question: Which cytogenetic alteration characterizes Burkitt lymphoma?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: This translocation places c-myc on chromosome 8 with the heavy-chain locus on chromosome 14, promoting dysregulated cellular growth and metabolism.
This alteration characterizes follicular lymphoma. It would be correct for painless waxing and waning adenopathy with preserved follicular architecture.
This alteration characterizes mantle cell lymphoma. It would be correct in an older man with advanced marrow and peripheral blood involvement.
This alteration occurs in approximately half of MALT lymphomas. It would fit lymphoma arising with chronic inflammation.
Bcl-6 alterations are associated with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Large heterogeneous cells with prominent nucleoli would support that choice.

question: Which biopsy finding establishes the diagnosis of Hodgkin lymphoma?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Monocytoid cells with large nuclei support marginal zone lymphoma. Chronic gastritis or Sjogren syndrome would make this finding applicable.
Reed-Sternberg cells in an excised involved lymph node establish Hodgkin lymphoma in the appropriate clinical setting.
Macrophages containing phagocytosed cells create the starry-sky appearance of Burkitt lymphoma. Rapid tumor growth would make this choice correct.
Cells with irregular and occasionally cleaved nuclei support mantle cell lymphoma. A t(11;14) alteration would make this finding correct.
Heterogeneous large cells with prominent nucleoli support diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. An aggressive adult lymphoma would fit that finding.

question: Which lymphoma is associated with t(11;14) and cyclin D1 dysregulation?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Follicular lymphoma is associated with t(14;18) and Bcl-2. That diagnosis would fit preserved follicles and waxing and waning adenopathy.
MALT-type marginal zone lymphoma may carry t(11;18). Chronic inflammatory disease would support that diagnosis.
Mantle cell lymphoma is highly associated with t(11;14), which dysregulates cyclin D1 and thereby affects coordination of mitosis.
Burkitt lymphoma carries t(8;14) involving c-myc. A rapidly doubling tumor with starry-sky histology would support it.
Hodgkin lymphoma is identified by Reed-Sternberg cells rather than this translocation. Contiguous nodal spread would favor Hodgkin lymphoma.

question: Which condition is caused by monoclonal proliferation of post-thymic CD4+ cells following viral infection?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following T-cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Primary CNS lymphoma is associated with EBV and HIV rather than HTLV-driven CD4+ proliferation. A ring-enhancing lesion with CD4 count below 50 would support it.
Mycosis fungoides presents with chronic progressing cutaneous lesions, and its genetics are not well understood. Patch-to-plaque progression would support it.
Mantle cell lymphoma is a mature B-cell neoplasm associated with t(11;14). Cyclin D1 dysregulation would support it.
HTLV causes monoclonal proliferation of post-thymic CD4+ cells, producing adult T-cell lymphoma.
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is a B-cell tumor associated with Bcl-2 and Bcl-6 alterations. Large nucleolated cells would support it.

question: A neoplasm grows slowly, may remain untreated initially, and is generally less responsive to therapy. Which disease behavior best matches these features?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Aggressive lymphomas grow rapidly, require immediate treatment, and are generally more treatment-responsive. Those features would make this choice correct.
The material links aggressive behavior with faster growth and general curability, not slow growth and delayed treatment. Rapid progression would support aggressive behavior.
Localization and immediate curability do not define the described disease behavior. Early localized MALT lymphoma would better fit a localized process.
A uniformly curable moderate category is not supported. Mantle cell lymphoma has a variable course and noncurative chemotherapy.
Indolent lymphomas grow slowly, may be observed initially, respond less readily to treatment, and are generally incurable despite a better prognosis.

question: A lymph node shows preserved follicular architecture, and cytogenetic analysis demonstrates juxtaposition of an immunoglobulin locus with an apoptosis-regulating gene. Which alteration is expected?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Preserved follicular architecture indicates follicular lymphoma, in which t(14;18) joins IGH on chromosome 14 with Bcl-2 on chromosome 18.
This alteration drives Burkitt lymphoma rather than follicular lymphoma. Starry-sky histology and extremely rapid growth would make it correct.
This alteration is characteristic of mantle cell lymphoma. Irregular cleaved nuclei and advanced marrow involvement would support that choice.
This alteration occurs in a subset of MALT lymphomas. Chronic gastritis or Sjogren syndrome would make it applicable.
Bcl-6 alteration is associated with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Large heterogeneous nucleolated cells would support it.

question: Which pairing correctly contrasts the usual dissemination patterns of Hodgkin lymphoma and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: This reverses the characteristic contrast. Hodgkin lymphoma first spreads contiguously, whereas diffuse large B-cell lymphoma commonly has extranodal involvement.
Hodgkin lymphoma usually spreads to contiguous lymph nodes, while diffuse large B-cell lymphoma commonly involves extranodal sites including marrow and CNS.
Progressive cutaneous involvement characterizes mycosis fungoides rather than Hodgkin lymphoma. Patches progressing to plaques would support cutaneous spread.
This does not capture the usual Hodgkin pattern, and cutaneous progression is linked to mycosis fungoides. Chronic skin lesions would support the second pattern.
Neither disease is defined by marrow-limited spread. Advanced mantle cell lymphoma commonly includes marrow and peripheral blood involvement.

question: An indolent lymphoma is linked to chronic inflammatory states and may arise in mucosal lymphoid tissue. Which associated alteration best supports this classification?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: This is the defining alteration of Burkitt lymphoma, an aggressive neoplasm. A jaw mass or massive abdominal disease would support it.
This supports follicular lymphoma rather than marginal zone lymphoma. Waxing and waning painless nodes would favor follicular lymphoma.
Approximately half of MALT lymphoma patients have t(11;18), which encodes proteins affecting lymphocyte apoptosis and proliferation.
This supports mantle cell lymphoma. Presentation in an older man with advanced marrow disease would make it correct.
Bcl-6 alteration supports diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Aggressive disease with prominent nucleoli would fit that alteration.

question: A lymphoid malignancy is generally incurable, has a long natural history, and transforms into an aggressive large-cell neoplasm at approximately 3% per year. Which diagnosis fits this course?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Mantle cell lymphoma is noncurable with chemotherapy but is not assigned the stated annual transformation pattern. t(11;14) would support mantle cell lymphoma.
Marginal zone lymphoma is often localized and slow-growing with an excellent prognosis. Chronic inflammatory disease would support it.
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is already aggressive and is cured in many patients. Large heterogeneous cells would support it.
Follicular lymphoma has a long, generally incurable course and transforms to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma at about 3% per year.
Burkitt lymphoma is rapidly aggressive but highly chemotherapy-sensitive. A doubling time below 24 hours would support it.

question: A lymphoma is highly aggressive yet can be cured in 70-80% of patients when treatment is prompt. Which therapeutic principle explains this apparent contrast?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Observation is appropriate for selected indolent lymphomas, not this rapidly growing disease. Asymptomatic follicular lymphoma would support observation.
The described lymphoma spreads rapidly to extranodal sites, so radiation alone is not the stated therapeutic principle. Early localized cutaneous disease would better support radiation.
The material does not identify transplantation as the explanation for prompt cure in this lymphoma. Refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma may prompt transplant consideration.
Slow growth and delayed therapy characterize indolent disease. Follicular lymphoma without treatment indications would fit this principle.
Burkitt lymphoma combines extremely rapid growth with marked sensitivity to aggressive chemotherapy, permitting cure when treatment is prompt.

question: Which paired findings most strongly distinguish adult T-cell lymphoma from primary CNS lymphoma?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following T-cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Adult T-cell lymphoma features hypercalcemia and lymphocytosis with lobulated flower cells, reflecting HTLV-driven CD4+ proliferation.
Seizures and large aggressive cells support primary CNS lymphoma. A ring-enhancing brain lesion would make this pair correct.
Memory loss and diagnostic CSF cytology are associated with primary CNS lymphoma rather than adult T-cell lymphoma. Severe immunosuppression would strengthen that diagnosis.
Generalized erythroderma with circulating tumor cells describes Sezary syndrome. Progressive mycosis fungoides would make this pair correct.
Plaques progressing to cutaneous tumors characterize mycosis fungoides. Chronic eczema-like lesions would support that choice.

question: Which pairing correctly connects an indolent lymphoma with an accepted initial management strategy?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Burkitt lymphoma requires prompt aggressive chemotherapy because its doubling time is below 24 hours. Untreated asymptomatic follicular lymphoma would support observation.
Observation is reasonable for follicular lymphoma without treatment indications, and patients may remain untreated for years.
Hodgkin lymphoma is managed with chemotherapy, radiation, or transplantation rather than bacterial eradication. Early H. pylori-positive MALT lymphoma would fit antibiotics.
Chemotherapy can modify mantle cell lymphoma but is not curative. Curative chemotherapy is more consistent with many aggressive lymphomas.
Primary CNS lymphoma in HIV is treated with HAART, chemotherapy, and whole-brain radiation. Early localized mycosis fungoides would fit localized radiation.

question: An HIV-associated neoplasm and an extremely fast-growing pediatric neoplasm share a viral association. Which virus is common to both?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: HIV is epidemiologically associated with primary CNS lymphoma but is not the shared viral association stated for Burkitt lymphoma. Severe immunosuppression would support HIV as the host condition.
HTLV causes adult T-cell lymphoma rather than either B-cell neoplasm. Hypercalcemia and flower cells would support HTLV.
Both Burkitt lymphoma and primary CNS lymphoma are associated with EBV infection.
H. pylori is linked to gastric MALT lymphoma and guides antibiotic treatment. Chronic gastritis would support this association.
This is not the specific shared virus. A chronic inflammatory state would instead support marginal zone lymphoma.

question: Which combination distinguishes mantle cell lymphoma from follicular lymphoma?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: This combination identifies follicular lymphoma. Waxing and waning painless adenopathy would make it correct.
This combination identifies Burkitt lymphoma. A rapidly enlarging jaw or abdominal tumor would support it.
This combination supports MALT-type marginal zone lymphoma. Chronic gastritis or Sjogren syndrome would make it correct.
Mantle cell lymphoma combines t(11;14)-mediated cyclin D1 dysregulation with irregular, occasionally cleaved nuclei.
This combination supports diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Aggressive advanced adult disease would make it correct.

question: Which progression correctly links an indolent cutaneous T-cell process to its advanced leukemic form?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following T-cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Marrow failure is not the described final progression of the cutaneous process. Cytopenias from marrow infiltration would support advanced follicular lymphoma treatment.
Jaw tumors characterize endemic Burkitt lymphoma rather than cutaneous T-cell disease. Rapid facial growth would support that diagnosis.
Ring-enhancing CNS lesions characterize primary CNS lymphoma. Severe HIV-associated immunosuppression would support that progression.
Flower cells occur in adult T-cell lymphoma rather than Sezary syndrome. HTLV-associated hypercalcemia would make this choice applicable.
Mycosis fungoides progresses from patches to plaques and tumors, with final progression to Sezary syndrome and generalized erythroderma.

question: A 32-year-old woman has a painless cervical mass without fever, night sweats, or weight loss. Tissue sampling suggests a lymphoid malignancy but does not preserve nodal architecture. Which next diagnostic step is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Definitive lymphoma diagnosis commonly requires excision of an involved node so architecture and diagnostic cells can be assessed.
Treatment should follow definitive classification rather than an architecture-limited sample. Confirmed aggressive lymphoma would make prompt chemotherapy appropriate.
Observation is reasonable for selected confirmed indolent disease, not an enlarging undiagnosed mass. Asymptomatic established follicular lymphoma would support observation.
Whole-brain radiation is used for primary CNS lymphoma, not isolated cervical adenopathy. A biopsied CNS lesion would make it applicable.
Antibiotic eradication is first-line for early H. pylori-positive MALT lymphoma. Chronic gastritis with confirmed MALT disease would support it.

question: A 68-year-old woman has painless waxing and waning epitrochlear adenopathy without constitutional symptoms. Biopsy preserves nodal follicles. Which molecular abnormality most likely underlies this process?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: This alteration produces Burkitt lymphoma, which is rapidly aggressive rather than waxing and waning. Starry-sky histology would make it correct.
The presentation and preserved follicles identify follicular lymphoma, driven by t(14;18) joining Bcl-2 and IGH.
This t(11;14) alteration identifies mantle cell lymphoma. Advanced disease in an older man would support it.
Bcl-6 alteration is associated with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Large heterogeneous nucleolated cells would make it correct.
This alteration supports MALT lymphoma. Chronic gastritis or Sjogren syndrome would make it applicable.

question: A 20-year-old man develops a rapidly enlarging abdominal mass and massive ascites. Biopsy shows medium-sized cells interspersed with macrophages containing phagocytosed debris. Which management approach is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Observation is inappropriate for a tumor that may double in less than 24 hours. Asymptomatic follicular lymphoma would make observation reasonable.
The abdominal and potentially extranodal dissemination requires systemic therapy. Early localized mycosis fungoides would support radiation alone.
The presentation and starry-sky pattern indicate Burkitt lymphoma, which is highly sensitive to aggressive chemotherapy and requires prompt treatment.
Antibiotic eradication treats early H. pylori-positive MALT lymphoma. Chronic gastritis with localized MALT disease would support it.
Transplantation is not the stated initial treatment for Burkitt lymphoma. Eligible patients with recurrent diffuse large B-cell lymphoma may receive autologous transplantation.

question: A 64-year-old man has fatigue, weight loss, and an enlarging nodal mass. Biopsy demonstrates heterogeneous large cells with prominent nucleoli. Which treatment strategy best matches the expected disease behavior?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Observation fits selected indolent lymphoma, not aggressive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Stable asymptomatic follicular lymphoma would support it.
This strategy is appropriate for early H. pylori-positive MALT lymphoma. Chronic gastritis and localized disease would make it correct.
Skin-directed radiation is used for early localized mycosis fungoides. Chronic localized patches would support it.
The histology and age indicate diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, an aggressive but potentially curable disease treated with combination chemotherapy and biologic therapy.
Untreated aggressive lymphoma has a poor prognosis and requires immediate therapy. A nonprogressive indolent process might permit observation, not supportive care alone.

question: A 70-year-old man has lymphadenopathy, marrow involvement, and circulating malignant cells. Biopsy shows irregular, occasionally cleaved nuclei. Which molecular event most likely drives the disease?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: c-myc activation through t(8;14) drives Burkitt lymphoma. A tumor doubling in under 24 hours would support it.
Bcl-2 involvement through t(14;18) characterizes follicular lymphoma. Preserved follicles would make it correct.
Bcl-6 alteration is associated with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Prominent nucleoli in heterogeneous large cells would support it.
This alteration occurs in MALT lymphoma. Chronic gastritis or Sjogren syndrome would make it applicable.
The advanced presentation, older male demographic, and cleaved nuclei indicate mantle cell lymphoma, driven by t(11;14)-mediated cyclin D1 dysregulation.

question: A 58-year-old woman with chronic gastritis has a localized gastric lymphoid tumor and evidence of active H. pylori infection. Which next management step is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Early H. pylori-positive MALT lymphoma is treated first with antibiotics directed at eradicating the associated infection.
Aggressive chemotherapy is not the first-line approach for early infection-associated MALT lymphoma. Burkitt lymphoma would require prompt aggressive chemotherapy.
Autologous transplantation is not first-line therapy for localized MALT lymphoma. Eligible patients with recurrent diffuse large B-cell lymphoma may receive it.
Whole-brain radiation applies to primary CNS lymphoma. A ring-enhancing cerebral lesion would make it relevant.
Observation alone leaves the identified inflammatory driver untreated. Observation is more appropriate for asymptomatic follicular lymphoma without treatment indications.

question: A 41-year-old man from the Caribbean presents after a 2-week decline with skin lesions and lytic bone lesions. Calcium is 13.1 mg/dL [8.5-10.5 mg/dL]. Which additional finding most strongly supports the diagnosis?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following T-cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Tingible-body macrophages support Burkitt lymphoma. A rapidly enlarging jaw or abdominal mass would make this finding correct.
The geographic association, hypercalcemia, skin and bone lesions indicate adult T-cell lymphoma, which shows lobulated flower cells.
This histology supports diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. An aggressive nodal or extranodal mass in an older adult would fit it.
These cells support marginal zone lymphoma. Chronic gastritis or Sjogren syndrome would make them relevant.
These cells support mantle cell lymphoma. t(11;14) with marrow involvement would make this finding correct.

question: A 39-year-old woman has chronic eczema-like patches that progress to plaques and cutaneous tumors. She later develops generalized erythroderma and circulating malignant cells. Which disease stage is now present?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following T-cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Adult T-cell lymphoma presents with HTLV-associated hypercalcemia, lytic lesions, and flower cells. Those findings would make this choice correct.
Localized disease does not include generalized erythroderma and circulating tumor cells. Confined patches would support this stage.
Generalized erythroderma with circulating tumor cells represents final progression of mycosis fungoides to Sezary syndrome.
Primary CNS lymphoma causes neurologic symptoms and a ring-enhancing lesion. Seizures with severe HIV-associated immunosuppression would support it.
Marginal zone lymphoma is associated with chronic inflammation but not this ordered cutaneous progression. Chronic gastritis with MALT disease would support it.

question: A 36-year-old man with HIV develops confusion and seizures. CD4+ count is 34 cells/mm3 [500-1500 cells/mm3], and imaging shows a ring-enhancing brain lesion. Which diagnostic procedure best establishes the suspected malignancy?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: No peripheral nodal target is described, and primary CNS disease requires direct CNS evaluation. Cervical adenopathy suspicious for Hodgkin lymphoma would support node excision.
Gastric biopsy would evaluate MALT lymphoma. Chronic gastritis with a gastric lesion would make it appropriate.
A smear can contribute to an initial hematologic evaluation but does not establish this focal CNS malignancy. Circulating flower cells would support adult T-cell lymphoma.
Primary CNS lymphoma is established by stereotactic brain biopsy showing large aggressive cells; CSF cytology may also contribute.
Skin biopsy evaluates mycosis fungoides, although early specimens can be difficult to interpret. Progressive patches and plaques would support it.

question: A patient with HIV has biopsy-confirmed primary CNS lymphoma. Which treatment combination best matches the general management strategy?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Antibiotic eradication is used for early H. pylori-positive MALT lymphoma, not primary CNS lymphoma. A localized gastric tumor would support that approach.
These modalities are listed for adult T-cell lymphoma. HTLV-associated flower cells and hypercalcemia would make this combination applicable.
These modalities are used across stages of mycosis fungoides. Progressive cutaneous patches and plaques would support them.
Observation is not appropriate for symptomatic primary CNS lymphoma. Selected follicular lymphoma can be observed, while transplant may be used in recurrent diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
HIV-associated primary CNS lymphoma is managed with HAART, chemotherapy, and whole-brain radiation therapy.

question: A 57-year-old woman with known follicular lymphoma develops rapidly enlarging nodes and a marked change in disease tempo. Which development is most concerning?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.text: Transformation to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
options.rationale: Follicular lymphoma transforms to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma at approximately 3% per year, and a sudden acceleration in tempo is concerning for this event.
MALT lymphoma arises with chronic inflammatory states rather than as the described transformation. Chronic gastritis with localized gastric disease would support it.
Mantle cell lymphoma is a distinct t(11;14)-associated neoplasm, not the stated transformation of follicular lymphoma. Cyclin D1 dysregulation would support it.
The stated transformation is into diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not Hodgkin lymphoma. Reed-Sternberg cells would support Hodgkin lymphoma.
Primary CNS lymphoma is associated with HIV, severe immunosuppression, and EBV rather than this disease-tempo change. A ring-enhancing lesion would support it.

question: A 66-year-old man has confirmed follicular lymphoma without constitutional symptoms, cytopenias, bulky disease, organ threat, or symptomatic extranodal involvement. Which next step is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Immediate treatment is not required without a clear indication in indolent follicular lymphoma. Burkitt lymphoma would require aggressive chemotherapy.
Observation is reasonable for asymptomatic follicular lymphoma without treatment indications, and treatment may be deferred for years.
Antibiotic eradication treats early H. pylori-positive MALT lymphoma. Confirmed gastric MALT disease would make it correct.
Whole-brain radiation treats primary CNS lymphoma. Neurologic symptoms with a biopsied CNS lesion would support it.
Transplantation is not indicated for stable untreated follicular lymphoma. Eligible recurrent diffuse large B-cell lymphoma may warrant this intervention.

question: A patient with previously observed follicular lymphoma develops progressive bulky nodes compressing a normal organ. Which management change is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Organ threat from progressive bulky disease is a clear indication to end observation. Stable asymptomatic disease would support continued observation.
Antibiotics are first-line for early H. pylori-positive MALT lymphoma, not progressive follicular lymphoma. Active gastric infection would support them.
Progressive bulky disease threatening an organ is a clear treatment indication in follicular lymphoma.
Phototherapy is an option for advanced mycosis fungoides, not bulky nodal follicular lymphoma. Progressive cutaneous plaques would support it.
HAART is part of management for HIV-associated primary CNS lymphoma. Severe HIV immunosuppression with a CNS lesion would support it.

question: A 29-year-old man has a jaw mass that enlarges dramatically over one day. Biopsy reveals a starry-sky pattern. Which cellular consequence most directly follows from the defining chromosomal alteration?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Cyclin D1 coordinates mitosis and is dysregulated in mantle cell lymphoma. t(11;14) would make this consequence correct.
Bcl-2 regulates apoptosis and is involved in follicular lymphoma. t(14;18) with preserved follicles would support this mechanism.
Proteins regulating apoptosis and proliferation are affected by t(11;18) in MALT lymphoma. Chronic gastritis would support it.
The presentation indicates Burkitt lymphoma. Its t(8;14) activates c-myc, a master oncogene regulating cellular growth and metabolism.
HTLV causes monoclonal CD4+ proliferation in adult T-cell lymphoma. Hypercalcemia and flower cells would support this mechanism.

question: A 52-year-old patient with Hodgkin lymphoma has constitutional symptoms, bulky adenopathy, and an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate. Which prognostic interpretation is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: The listed findings increase rather than reduce relapse risk. Younger age without constitutional symptoms or bulky disease would indicate fewer adverse factors.
Although Hodgkin lymphoma has a generally good prognosis, no combination guarantees cure. Absence of relapse factors would still not establish certainty.
Confirmed Hodgkin lymphoma is treated with chemotherapy, radiation, or transplantation rather than observation alone. Selected asymptomatic follicular lymphoma may be observed.
The listed factors indicate relapse risk, not transformation into indolent disease. Follicular lymphoma instead may transform into aggressive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
Age over 40, constitutional symptoms, high ESR, and bulky adenopathy are all listed factors that increase the risk of Hodgkin lymphoma relapse.

question: A 44-year-old man has hypotension, acute kidney dysfunction, and findings concerning for a lymphoid malignancy. Which next step is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical manifestations, epidemiology, cytogenetics, general treatment and general prognosis of the following B cell lymphomas.

options.rationale: Hemodynamic instability and renal failure are indications for hospitalization with stat consultation when leukemia or lymphoma is suspected.
Routine observation is unsafe in hemodynamic instability with renal dysfunction. A stable patient without emergency findings could undergo outpatient evaluation.
Skin biopsy applies to suspected mycosis fungoides but does not address this emergency. Chronic progressive skin lesions would support that procedure.
Radiation requires an established diagnosis and appropriate disease site. Early localized mycosis fungoides would support localized radiation.
H. pylori eradication treats confirmed early gastric MALT lymphoma, not undifferentiated unstable disease. Localized infection-associated gastric lymphoma would support it.
